basic_info.name: EkaScribe and Eka Care
basic_info.description: Eka Care is an India-first, ABDM-native health software platform operated by Orbi Health Private Limited (Bengaluru) that bundles a doctor-facing ambient AI scribe (EkaScribe), a clinician EMR (EkaDoc), a patient personal health record with a Medical Records Analyser that OCRs prescriptions and lab reports into structured data and links them to SNOMED CT and LOINC, and developer APIs including an ABDM Connect suite that implements ABDM milestones M1-M4 as both HIP and HIU. The single most load-bearing fact for MediKiosk Module C is that EkaScribe already emits its structured clinical notes as a FHIR bundle (via a session API implementing the MedScribeAlliance Protocol v0.1 with caller-selectable templates and whitelisted output languages), proving that an Indian vendor can go from raw multilingual code-mixed consultation audio to a structured, EMR-ready, FHIR-shaped note on production scale (vendor reports 1M+ EkaScribe sessions, 140M+ records managed, 33K+ clinics and 90K+ doctors) - but it does so cloud-first and in a doctor-side, during-visit workflow, not as an offline, patient-elicited, pre-consultation OPConsultRecord.
basic_info.organization: Eka Care (legal entity Orbi Health Private Limited), Bengaluru, India; founded 2020 by Vikalp Sahni, Deepak Tuli and Abhishek Begerhotta

technical_features.what_it_does: EkaScribe records or accepts a doctor-patient consultation (live mic, uploaded audio, or an already-produced transcript) and returns a structured clinical document - SOAP note, clinical notes or EMR-template output - in seconds, with speaker diarization, custom specialty templates, a 'learn my style' adaptation from physician edits, and an optional codification flag; the EkaScribe API surfaces the finished note as a FHIR bundle via a session protocol (MedScribeAlliance v0.1) and can translate a transcript into a target Indian language instead of structuring it. On the patient side, Eka Care PHR ingests documents and synchronises records, and the Medical Records Analyser converts prescriptions and multi-page lab reports into structured entities, linking them to SNOMED-CT and LOINC; Eka also runs a Clinical Decision Support System that reasons over longitudinal records to surface drug-interaction and investigation prompts during consultations, and ABDM Connect APIs handle ABHA, care-context linking, consent and HPR/HFR registration.
technical_features.architecture: Cloud-first, API/webhook architecture. ASR is powered by Eka's in-house 'Parrotlet' family of Indian medical speech models (Parrotlet-a 2 Pro released Feb 2026 with 5B parameters; Parrotlet-a 2.5 Pro benchmarked Aug 2026), chosen via a pro/lite model picker - 'pro' adds speaker diarization, custom templates and 60-minute sessions, 'lite' is a fast dictation mode. The EkaScribe flow is session-based and asynchronous (create session -> stream audio chunks or upload transcript -> end session -> poll/get structured document), with webhooks for completion. Records analysis uses OCR plus in-house LLMs for handwritten multilingual Indian documents, followed by terminology linking to SNOMED-CT and LOINC. Delivery runs on AWS/Google cloud with India-hosted infrastructure. No architecture detail is published on the exact note-generation LLM or the summarisation stage.
technical_features.inputs: Doctor-patient consultation audio (live or uploaded), pre-existing transcripts, doctor/patient/visit context metadata, medical specialty, input and output language selection, and templates; on the patient side, photographed or uploaded prescriptions, lab reports, discharge summaries and insurance documents, synced Gmail/WhatsApp records and Apple Health / Health Connect data; ABDM-linked longitudinal records via consent.
technical_features.outputs: Structured SOAP / clinical notes and EMR-template documents; prescriptions; clinical summaries; a session document returned via API that is described as a FHIR bundle for interoperability; PDF prescription exports; translated transcripts (eng, hi, ta, te, bn, mr, gu, kn, ml, pa, as); parser outputs of lab reports as structured observations with LOINC mapping and prescriptions with SNOMED-CT/CDCI-style coding. On the ABDM side, ABHA IDs, linked care contexts and consent records.
technical_features.standards_compliance: Claims and badges: ABDM Compliant, FHIR Compliant, NHA Approved, HIPAA, ISO 27001 certified, AWS Secured and Google Partner (episode site); the ABDM Connect API documents HIP and HIU roles and coverage of ABDM milestones M1 (ABHA identity), M2 (care-context linking and data sharing), M3 (consent management and FHIR data fetch) and M4 (HPR/HFR registration), plus the separate PHR-app track (Scan & Share, Health Locker). The EkaScribe API states notes are available as a FHIR bundle, but Eka does not publicly enumerate which NRCeS/ABDM profiles (e.g. OPConsultRecord v6.5.0/v7.0.0) the emitted bundle validates against - conformance is claimed, and the FHIR-bundle output shape is documented, but profile-level validation evidence was not found. SNOMED-CT and LOINC are used on the records-analyser pipeline. No statement found that the scribe note is emitted as an OPConsultRecord Composition with a physician attester. [Profile-level NRCeS conformance: uncertain]
technical_features.offline_capability: Cloud-first by default: EkaScribe is a web/Chrome-extension product and the site states all audio and text data is encrypted in transit and at rest and hosted on HIPAA-compliant cloud servers located in India. Offline capability was announced but is not yet a shipping feature: in Feb 2026 Eka Care announced an NVIDIA collaboration to build 'India's first offline-capable, unified medical scribe' with a variant designed to run entirely on a doctor's mobile device using NVIDIA's AI stack (NeMo Curator and Nemotron/Parakeet speech models), explicitly framed as future/development work. Eka later said NeMo Curator is used to curate Indian medical conversation data and that it is evaluating NVIDIA Nemotron Speech / Parakeet ASR, aiming to merge ASR and LLM into one architecture; no shipped offline build was confirmed in this pass. On the patient PHR, a 'Secret Locker' stores selected sensitive documents only on the device. [Offline scribe production availability: uncertain]
technical_features.languages_supported: EkaScribe markets support for 20+ languages including English, Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Urdu and more; API enums expose en-IN, en-US, hi, gu, kn, ml, ta, te, bn, mr, pa and or (Odia) for input/output, and translation targets also include Assamese (as). The company explicitly positions code-mixed Hindi/Hinglish and regional accents as core competence, and the Parrotlet models are marketed for Indian English and Hindi clinical speech. Devanagari-script rendering for output is implied by the Hindi/Odia/Marathi support but the exact bilingual (English + Devanagari side-by-side) rendering format was not documented.
technical_features.deployment_model: Cloud SaaS with web app, Chrome extension for one-click insertion into web-based EMRs (copy/paste fallback for offline EMR systems), iOS/Android apps and a WhatsApp-based entry point; developer REST APIs with API-key/OAuth authentication and pay-per-use billing. Data hosted on India-located HIPAA-compliant cloud servers. The announced offline variant targets a doctor's mobile device; no kiosk or fixed-hardware product exists. Exact server hardware or GPU requirements are not published.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: EkaScribe does not publish a summary/note-generation accuracy (no ROUGE/BERTScore/clinical-fact recall), so the load-bearing quality numbers are ASR-level and vendor-run. The Eka medical-scribe developer page publishes a word-error-rate table on an in-house curated benchmark (overall WER: Parrotlet-A 0.29 vs Whisper V3 Base 0.42, AWS Transcribe 0.52, Wav2Vec 0.56, AWS Custom 0.43; category-level e.g. top_50k_meds 0.23 vs 0.39). The Parrotlet-a 2 Pro / v2 launch cites medical keyword accuracy of ~93% in Indian English and ~85% in Hindi, a phantom-speech (hallucinated speech on noise-only audio) rate of 3%, lowest reported semantic WER of 0.10 on Indian English and 0.20 on Hindi, and 15-20% higher medical keyword accuracy than Sarvam Saaras V3 and ElevenLabs Scribe V2 on drugs/diagnostic entities. The open-weight Parrotlet-a-en-5b model reports WER 0.109 / CER 0.047 / semWER 0.072 / kwWER 0.062 on the Eka Medical ASR English benchmark, ahead of GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0/2.5 Flash, Whisper V3 large, Bhashini ASR and ElevenLabs Scribe V1. All figures are vendor-produced on proprietary/internal evaluation sets. [Note-generation (summary) accuracy metrics: uncertain - not published]
performance_metrics.latency: Vendor-stated sub-second ASR inference for Parrotlet-a v2, described as up to ~30x faster than large reasoning models (on the same clip, Gemini 3 Pro with thinking-high reportedly needed 30+ seconds), and note generation 'in seconds'. The EkaScribe API is asynchronous: template generation starts in the background (returning 202) and clients poll ~1 second until the document status is success - so human-perceived time-to-note is seconds but not a fixed published SLA. No hardware context is given for the latency claims (cloud GPU assumed). [Exact end-to-end time-to-summary on given hardware: uncertain]
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: The Parrotlet-a 2 Pro/V2 ASR model is a compact 5-billion-parameter architecture, marketed as balancing speed, cost and capability and specifically as efficient enough to run on a doctor's mobile device in the announced offline variant (Eka says the lightweight projection-layer-only training minimises compute and supports resource-constrained, real-time use). The open-weight Parrotlet-a-en-5b is released publicly. No RAM, storage, VRAM or CPU/GPU floor is published for EkaScribe itself, and Eka's own scribe production runs in the cloud. [Exact RAM/CPU footprint for the offline variant: uncertain]
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: Vendor homepage (fetched 2026-09-16): 33K+ clinics/hospitals onboarded, 90K+ doctors onboarded, 20Mn+ ABHA created, 140Mn+ records managed, 8Mn+ MedAssist agent-bot conversations, 1Mn+ EkaScribe sessions. EkaScribe sub-site states 1400+ active users worldwide and a 4.8/5 rating from 500+ doctors, and claims 12+ hours/week saved and 80% admin workload reduction; a Feb 2026 press item said Parrotlet-a v2 powers EkaScribe used by 'more than 3,000 doctors' (the count is inconsistent across pages, so treat the scribe seat count as approximate). ABDM-side: ~1.8 crore ABHA IDs generated, ~2.85 crore health records linked, ~58 lakh Scan & Share transactions, ~3,500 doctors registered in ABDM via Eka, ~3,150+ HFRs, record-linkage success above 93% in 2025 (peaking ~97%). Eka states ~12,000 paid doctors in 2025 with a target of 35,000-40,000 and 160+ developer/enterprise API consumers.
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: Vendor-claimed and internal. ASR evaluation uses Eka's own curated Eka Medical ASR Evaluation Dataset (3,900+ recordings, ~3,600 English and ~320 Hindi, narrated medical entities/sentences and impromptu conversations, partly from five medical colleges) with WER/CER/semWER/kwWER metrics, and an in-house production-audio benchmark for the Parrotlet-a 2.x comparisons (KARMA evaluation toolkit referenced for earlier models). The dataset and some model weights are public (Hugging Face), which is more transparent than most peers, but the note-generation/summary quality has no published benchmark, no peer-reviewed evaluation, and no independent third-party validation was located. Accuracy numbers are vendor-produced on proprietary sets, so they establish relative ASR quality, not validated clinical-note correctness.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: Eka Care/EkaScribe is the closest deployed Indian prior art for the full Module C chain and simultaneously the strongest 'already done' threat and the best feasibility evidence. It validates that (a) Indian clinical speech can be transcribed at useful accuracy despite heavy noise and Hinglish code-mixing (Parrotlet WER ~0.29 overall; 93%/85% medical-keyword accuracy for Indian English/Hindi), (b) an Indian vendor can emit a structured note as a FHIR bundle and operate deep inside ABDM (HIP + HIU, M1-M4, consent), and (c) the market will pay per doctor (Rs 1,499/month) and per API minute. It threatens naive differentiation: 'we summarise multilingual Indian consultations into a structured note and push it to ABDM' is demonstrably buildable by a funded incumbent at 1M+ session scale. What Eka does NOT supply, and where Module C's gap remains real, is the patient-side, pre-consultation capture flow (EkaScribe listens during the doctor's visit), an offline-first on-prem/kiosk execution path (Eka is cloud and its offline mode is announced-not-shipped), and evidence of emitting a physician-attested NRCeS OPConsultRecord for the pre-visit history.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (1) the deterministic, template-driven output contract used by EkaScribe (create session -> structure into a named template -> return one structured document), which mirrors Module C's 'store fields once, render many' model and gives a clean API shape and webhook/poll pattern; (2) explicit target-language output selection with a fixed enum (including hi, mr, bn, ta, te, gu, kn, ml, pa, or) as a model for Module C bilingual rendering; (3) the openness strategy of publishing the ASR evaluation dataset and some model weights as credibility/ecosystem play; (4) their ABDM Connect milestone framing (M1-M4, HIP/HIU, Scan & Share, Health Locker) as the integration checklist Module D must satisfy. Adapt: Eka's ASR benchmark methodology (WER + semWER + medical-keyword WER, plus a 'phantom speech' hallucination-on-noise metric at 3%) is directly reusable as Module C's ASR quality gate - adopt the phantom-speech metric explicitly. Reject: cloud-only execution and the announced-but-unshipped offline model as a dependence; and note-generation without published fidelity metrics - Module C should not copy the pattern of shipping a note generator with zero published summary-accuracy evidence, because the SIH evaluation and the omission/hallucination literature make that a judge-visible weakness.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: Cloud-first and India cloud-hosted but internet-dependent - the offline variant is a Feb 2026 announcement still described as being built with NVIDIA, so Eka does not currently prove offline operation on constrained hardware. Doctor-side, during-visit workflow, so it does not demonstrate patient-elicited pre-consultation history or unattended capture. No published summary/note-generation accuracy, no peer-reviewed or independent evaluation, and all ASR numbers are vendor-run on internal sets (benchmarks are relative, not clinically validated). Documentation-level inefficiency: the scribe emits a 'FHIR bundle' but the ABDM profile it targets is not named, so NRCeS OPConsultRecord conformance and the mandatory attester are unproven. Adoption counts are inconsistent across Eka's own pages (1,400+ active scribe users vs 3,000+ doctors vs 1M+ sessions), and the pricing/seat model undercuts 'free' positioning. The Medical Records Analyser and Intelligent Patient Summaries are largely described at marketing altitude - parsing is documented, but no error rates for handwriting or the summariser are published.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: Strengthens MediKiosk's differentiation on exactly the axes Eka leaves open: (1) offline-first/on-prem kiosk - Eka is cloud and its offline mode is future work, so a genuinely offline, CPU/iGPU-only kiosk remains unclaimed; (2) patient-elicited pre-consultation history via voice+touch - Eka captures during the physician encounter, not before it, so the pre-visit structured HistoryBundle and the resulting physician-ready summary are not Eka's product; (3) named NRCeS OPConsultRecord emission with a physician attester - Eka claims generic FHIR/ABDM compliance but does not document OPConsultRecord profile validation. Erodes/weakens: the claim that only MediKiosk can produce multilingual Indian clinical summaries is false - Eka has better ASR evidence than most. Net: Eka narrows the 'can an Indian vendor do structured multilingual clinical notes + ABDM?' question to 'yes, if cloud', so MediKiosk must win on offline execution, patient-side elicitation and a hard NRCeS/attestation contract rather than on multilingual summarisation existing.

business_info.license: Proprietary commercial software; source is closed and no open-source license applies to the platform. Partial exception: Eka Care has released some Parrotlet model weights openly (Parrotlet-a-en-5b English ASR on Hugging Face, plus 'Parrotlet open models' for medical document intelligence announced 2026-08-10); the exact license terms of those open-weight releases were not captured in this pass. [Open-weight license terms: uncertain]
business_info.pricing: EkaScribe: Rs 1,499/month per doctor billed monthly (about Rs 50/day), annual billing saves ~17%; a free tier limits 5 consultations/day while Pro offers unlimited consultations; card payments (Visa/Mastercard/Amex) and 7-day refunds. Developer APIs are pay-per-use (Eka cites a per-minute charge for Scribe usage) with separate enterprise/ABDM Connect commercial terms. Eka EMR/other add-ons are quoted separately by sales.
business_info.funding: Total disclosed equity funding $19.5M across rounds: $4.5M seed (2021-07-19) and $15M Series A (2022-07-19, led by Hummingbird Ventures with 3one4Capital, Mirae Assets, Verlinvest, Aditya Birla Ventures, Binny Bansal, Rohit MA and others). TechCrunch reported management hinted at a post-money valuation 'closer to three-digit million dollars'; Tracxn lists a current valuation of about Rs 397 crore. PitchBook lists a later-stage VC round and a secondary transaction dated 2026-02-01 (amount undisclosed), suggesting recent internal/secondary activity. Revenue: reported near $3.5M ARR in 2025, targeting $10M ARR within 18-20 months; legal entity Orbi Health Pvt Ltd reported Rs 10-50 crore revenue as of FY2025.
business_info.commercial_status: Commercial, venture-backed private company (a paid product plus free tier and pay-per-use APIs), with strong public-sector alignment as an ABDM participant and an NVIDIA collaboration announcement. Not a government programme or unpaid project. The NVIDIA offline-scribe work is described as a partnership/development initiative, and Eka says it is exploring open-sourcing the consolidated offline model.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Domestic ambient-scribe and records digitisation competitors: Augnito Omni (doctor-side dictation + ambient EMR), Sunoh.ai (eClinicalWorks/healow, cloud ambient scribe also marketed in India), Practo/1mg/PharmEasy-adjacent record products (transaction-oriented rather than clinical documentation). International ambient scribes: Abridge, Microsoft/Nuance DAX Copilot, Ambience Healthcare, Nabla, DeepScribe, Commure Scribe. PHR/interoperability overlap: the ABDM PHR ecosystem, Google/other ABHA-linked apps. The direct Module C overlap is strongest with any product that converts consultation audio or documents into a structured FHIR/ABDM note, which today is EkaScribe, Augnito and the ABDM-native entrants, not the US kiosk/intake vendors.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: ABDM via Eka ABDM Connect as both HIP and HIU (ABHA creation/login, care-context linking, consent management, HPR/HFR, Scan & Share, Health Locker), plus UHI and NHCX expansion; Google Wallet ABHA (with ABDM guardrails); WhatsApp for scheduling/messaging; lab partners Evital, Orange Health and Metropolis; Apple Health and Android Health Connect; Chrome-extension and API integration into third-party EMRs/HIS (EMR-agnostic note insertion), and a developer portal with API keys, OAuth-style auth, webhooks and pay-per-use billing. EHR side: it is designed to insert into any web-based EMR and to export structured text/PDF otherwise.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: ABDM is the dominant tailwind: Eka's whole posture is ABDM-native, and it registers record-linkage success above 93% and participates in sandbox-to-production, UHI and NHCX expansion, which means the ABDM rails (ABHA, consent manager, HIP/HIU, FHIR R4) are mature enough for a kiosk product to target. Eka demonstrates that government-aligned procurement and public messaging (demonstrating EkaScribe live to the Prime Minister at the India AI Impact Summit 2026) are viable go-to-market channels for Indian clinical AI. At the same time, Eka is converging on MediKiosk's own feature space - it lists 'Intelligent Patient Summaries built from ABHA-linked histories' and pre-consult voice agents as in-progress - so the moat is narrowing and speed/positioning matter. DPDP compliance and India data residency are ecosystem-level requirements Eka advertises (India-hosted HIPAA servers, ISO 27001) and that MediKiosk must also meet.

history.release_date: Eka Care company founded 2020 (Orbi Health Pvt Ltd incorporated 2020-12-04); Eka PHR/ABDM products launched from 2021; EkaScribe emerged as the ambient AI scribe product from roughly 2024-2025 and is publicly sold on ekascribe.ai with API access documented from 2024-2025. [Exact first public EkaScribe release date: uncertain]
history.key_milestones: 2020 - founded (Vikalp Sahni, Deepak Tuli, Abhishek Begerhotta). 2021-07-19 - $4.5M seed. 2022-07-19 - $15M Series A led by Hummingbird Ventures. 2025-07 - releases Eka Medical ASR evaluation dataset and open-weight Parrotlet-a-en-5b/v-lite ASR models. 2025-08 - Economic Times reports 110M+ records digitised, 50M+ users, ~$3.5M ARR, 12,000 paid doctors. 2026-02-12 - Parrotlet-a 2 Pro launch (5B params, sub-second inference, 3% phantom speech). 2026-02-18 - NVIDIA partnership for an offline-capable unified medical scribe. 2026-02-24/03 - India AI Impact Summit 2026: EkaScribe demonstrated live to PM Modi, 600+ demos. 2026-08-10 - Parrotlet-a 2.5 Pro benchmark update and open-weight Parrotlet models for medical document intelligence.
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: Within the last six months (since ~2026-03-16): (1) 2026-08-10 - Parrotlet-a 2.5 Pro benchmark update released, continuing the ASR cadence. (2) 2026-08-10 - open-weight Parrotlet models for medical document intelligence released, advancing the open-models/‘build on us’ posture. (3) 2026-08-11/12 - Eka Care Add-ons launched, bundling clinic management, AI scribe, WhatsApp and payments into one platform. (4) The NVIDIA offline-scribe programme (announced Feb 2026) continued to be the headline roadmap item; no production offline release was confirmed in this window. (5) Eka continued ABDM expansion messaging (UHI, NHCX, PM-JAY integration) and lists 'Intelligent Patient Summaries built from ABHA-linked histories' as innovation-in-progress - i.e. Eka is now explicitly moving toward a patient-history summary, which is Module C's target. (6) Vendor homepage metrics updated to 1M+ EkaScribe sessions, 140M+ records managed, 33K+ clinics, 90K+ doctors. Exact content of the Parrotlet-a 2.5 Pro benchmark body could not be extracted (page renders dynamically); the release is confirmed but its detailed numbers are unverified. [Parrotlet-a 2.5 Pro benchmark details: uncertain]

market_positioning.target_users: Clinicians (solo and small clinics first, then hospitals and clinic chains), patients/families using the PHR, and developers/enterprises building on the APIs and ABDM Connect; secondarily insurers/payers and public-health programmes (NHCX, PM-JAY).
market_positioning.market_segment: Spans multiple segments: clinician EMR/EHR and ambient clinical documentation (EkaScribe/EkaDoc), patient-facing PHR and health-record digitisation (Eka Care app + Medical Records Analyser), clinical decision support, and health-data interoperability/ABDM tooling (ABDM Connect APIs). It is best described as an India-native, ABDM-anchored clinical AI and health-data platform rather than a diagnostics kiosk or AYUSH-specific tool.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: Eka pitches itself as 'the AI-Native Health OS' and 'India's fastest-growing connected healthcare platform', 'defining the AI-native health stack in India', building 'the digital backbone for doctors, hospitals, and patients through Eka EMR, Eka Scribe, Eka PHR, and Eka DevPortal'. EkaScribe is sold as a 'purpose-built AI scribe, not just a side project' with 'clinical-grade accuracy' and 'built to survive OPDs, not podcasts'. The NVIDIA work is framed as a 'sovereignty-first' model that can live on a doctor's mobile, independent of cloud connectivity.
